sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Characters of the subgenus Paracapritermes (this species is the type species of the subgenus): the soldier head has well-developed frontal projections which hide the fontanelle in dorsal view; the mandibles are asymmetrical, the left strongly twisted with a short blunt spine-like tooth at the base, the right shorter than the left, strongly curved but not twisted, with a small but distinct cleft at the base of the inner margin; antennae 14-segmented. The alate is not recorded in the original, which gives only a description of the dealated adult. This is a small dark brown species; the soldier has a pale yellow, slender head, the apex of the frontal projections turned upwards, and no lateral projections.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text:
The original records the alate as not seen (Not known) and describes only the dealated adult: a small dark brown species, the head and pronotum darkest, the postclypeus, antennae and abdominal tergites slightly paler, the legs mainly clay-coloured with the tibiae tinged with brown, the venter pale brown. Head small, almost not narrowing anteriorly, broadly rounded behind, rather flat on top, hairy. Compound eyes prominent (0.22×0.25). Ocelli small (length 0.09), far from the compound eyes, the inner margin slightly raised. Fontanelle slit-like, continued forwards as an indistinct secondary slit. Tooth 1 of the mandibles larger than tooth 2. Postclypeus 0.18 long and 0.40 wide at the base, the anterior margin slightly concave; anteclypeus almost as long as the postclypeus and projecting distinctly forwards. Labrum small, narrow at the base, widest at the middle, the apex bluntly rounded, not distinctly inflated. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 1 long and narrow; segment 2 about half of segment 1 and much narrower; segment 3 very short and narrow; segment 4 longer than segment 5 and as long as segment 6; segments 6—14 progressively longer; segment 15 shorter and narrower than segment 14, elongate oval, widest at the middle. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head, almost hemispherical, the anterior margin straight, the posterior margin with almost no notch, a pit-like impression on each side a short distance behind the anterior margin, nearer the mid-line than the lateral margin. Mesonotum and metanotum distinctly narrowed, the posterior margin deeply and sharply concave.
Measurements: length without wings 4.50 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.00 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.55 mm; head width 0.82 mm; pronotum length 0.47 mm; pronotum width 0.73 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head pale yellow, slender, the apex of the frontal projections turned upwards, without lateral projections. Right mandible shorter than the left, strongly curved but not twisted; left mandible strongly twisted, as in Capritermes. Labrum narrow, thick, the sides parallel, the anterolateral angles forming points, truncate between the two points. Postclypeus very narrow. In dorsal view of the head the fontanelle is hidden by the frontal projections. Antennae 14-segmented.
Measurements: body length 4.10—4.40 mm; head length (including mandibles) 2.01—2.38 mm; head length (to apex of frontal projections) 1.28—1.43 mm; head width 0.88—0.95 mm; pronotum length 0.25—0.27 mm; pronotum width 0.55 mm.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original gives it as Mirotermes (Paracapritermes) primus sp. nov. (the subgenus name in the heading was OCRed as 'PAR AO APR ITERMES'), and it is the type species of the subgenus Paracapritermes, with the type locality North Queensland: Mt. Molloy, also recorded from Clohesy River. The original has only the Dealated adult and Soldier sections, without descriptions of the alate and worker; the alate section is given as not seen after the statement in the original, and its content is the dealated adult. One soldier sentence reads in the original OCR: "Right mandible shorter than the left, strongly curved, but not twisted; the right mandible strongly twisted, as in Capritermes." The second "right" should be "left" and has been corrected from the subgenus character sentence ('the left mandible strongly twisted'), and the text above follows the left mandible. This is a homonym, not the same species as Cryptotermes primus. OCR misreadings: 'Pigsc'/'Pig.'='Figs.'/'Fig.', 'Dehind'='behind', 'l3t'='1st', 'sth'='5th', 'ap-ex'='apex', 'Lent upwards'='bent upwards', 'comers'='corners', 'man-dibles' broken across lines, '55' is OCR noise, 'Corynbosa'='corymbosa'.
